newsitem.title: IRAQ: Malaysian minister ends trade talks in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian minister ends trade talks in Iraq.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi left Baghdad on Tuesday after talks on expanding trade under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.
It said Badawi held discussions with Iraqi officials on enhancing economic and trade relations.
The official newspaper al-Qadissiya quoted Badawi as saying after meeting Iraqi Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh that Malaysia was ready to sell Iraq various goods.
Iraq imports most of its cooking oil from Malaysia.
Badawi also met President Saddam Hussein and Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed. Malaysia's oil firm Petronas is interested in Iraq's four-billion-barrel Ratawi oilfield.
